findings.summary: adopt() stages the adopted files with `git add -- <files>` but then runs `git commit` with no pathspec, so it commits the entire index. A change staged before the call whose working bytes equal HEAD is invisible to inspect() (which compares HEAD tree vs working tree, classifying it `clean`) and would be committed alongside the adopted append, outside the bytes bound by the confirmation token. Narrow, but it deviates from spec item 2's "adopts only the exact append-only bytes bound by that token"; committing with an explicit pathspec would close it.

No test guards the exact regression this development corrects: that serve() passes a concrete source into build_mcp_server rather than leaving work_folders=None. TestReconcileSourceBinding covers the governed_work_folder_store factory and a bound-but-unconfigured server, and the acceptance harness constructs GitWorkFolderSource directly, so nothing fails if the serve() wiring is later dropped and RECONCILE_SOURCE_UNBOUND returns in production.

The acceptance harness proves before/after byte identity for the stale-token and unsafe-residue scenarios only as a derived boolean (`bytes_unchanged`), not as raw echoed before/after bytes or digests. The invariant is genuinely enforced in-process and gates the exit code, but the printed evidence for that specific claim is a synthesized assertion rather than the raw payload the spec asks for.

Spec item 7 (merge/push to remote main via the governed dev-dispatch merger, with a merge/deployment receipt naming accepted commit, remote-main commit, production fast-forward status, and MCP restart/health) is not performed in this commit and cannot be, since it follows acceptance. The implement actor correctly did not fabricate an unobserved receipt. This APPROVE does not discharge item 7; it remains outstanding for the post-acceptance governed flow.

WorkFolderReconciler is constructed per server with an empty in-memory ledger, so replay idempotence is process-scoped. After a production restart, re-confirming an already-adopted token refuses with RECONCILE_REFUSED (the base has moved, so the token no longer binds) instead of replaying the sealed receipt. This is fail-closed -- nothing is adopted twice and history does not fork -- but it becomes an operationally visible behaviour now that a real source is actually bound.

The mandated `git diff --exit-code 56f50346 ea9fa287 -- . ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'` check could not be executed mechanically from this read-only seat (no shell or Git access). Product consistency was assessed by inspection instead: .git/HEAD is detached at ea9fa287, the checked-out tree carries the full implementation matching the implement handoff's verification record, and the only artifacts attributable to the review materialization (reviews/rc-e34f186c.../review.json and feedback/index.json) live under the reserved .dev-dispatch/ namespace. No evidence of a product-file change was found; the diff itself was not run.
